audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill / Warwick / Warwick / Skill / Skill / Warwick / Warwick — Warwick four stages, Trundle none — while Trundle wins 55.98% over 209 games and six of the seven whys describe Trundle winning that stage: "making every short trade a net positive for Trundle", "you walk him down on your own terrain", "he either eats another full exchange with zero sustain left", "Subjugate at level 6 is essentially an I-win button".
audit.why: This is the third entry in this slice where the stage labels contradict the paragraphs printed underneath them. 55.98% is one of Trundle's better lanes and the reason is on the page already — Chomp saps the AD his auto-attack drain pattern runs on, and Subjugate takes a cut of exactly the Bami's Cinder build Warwick commits to.
audit.corrected: Trundle from level 1 through first item; two-plus items to Skill, where whys[6] says Heartsteel scaling "can match" the R window rather than beat it.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] gives Infinite Duress a 1.8-second suppression. `mid` says "it has a long cooldown at early ranks" with no figure.
audit.why: Infinite Duress suppresses for 1.5 seconds and is 110/90/70 seconds. The 110 against Subjugate's 120 is the one number that decides the level-6 stage — his ultimate returns ten seconds sooner than yours, so the ranks he puts into it matter more than the ranks you put into anything. And Riot's text adds the detail nobody writes down: the leap scales with his bonus movement speed, which means Blood Hunt does not just make him faster, it makes his ultimate reach further.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress: 1.5s suppression, 110/90/70s, and the leap distance scales with his bonus move speed.

audit.whatIsWrong: `mid` says "his passive heals him far harder when you are low", wants.foe[1] says to land Infinite Duress "when you're below 50% HP so his passive healing and the suppression flip the fight", and wants.you[2] talks about "his Q Blood Hunt healing".
audit.why: Two different abilities read two different health bars and the page has merged them into one. Blood Hunt reads YOURS: it senses enemies below 50% health for move speed and attack speed, and triples at 25%. Eternal Hunger reads HIS: he heals for his bonus magic damage below 50% health, tripled below 25%. So the correct rule is not one line but two — stay above half to keep Blood Hunt switched off, and understand that a Warwick you have almost killed is the most dangerous Warwick on the map. Blood Hunt also has no healing component at all, so "Q Blood Hunt healing" names a thing twice over that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Blood Hunt keys off your health; Eternal Hunger keys off his and triples under 25%. Jaws of the Beast is the Q that heals.

audit.whatIsWrong: `early` ends "He has no dash to clear terrain", and both `early` and whys[2] tell the player Pillar of Ice makes him "take the knockup".
audit.why: Warwick has two dashes. Jaws of the Beast is a 365-range lunge on 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 seconds, and Infinite Duress is a leap. Telling a Trundle that the pillar is a cage against a champion who can dash out of it is the kind of line that loses a player the trade he was told he had won. Pillar of Ice also has no knock-up — it is impassable terrain plus a slow.
audit.corrected: Jaws of the Beast is a dash on 8s at rank 1; the pillar slows and redirects him rather than trapping him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl appears nowhere on the page, and Jaws of the Beast is never described as maximum-health damage.
audit.why: Primal Howl is 15/14/13/12/11 seconds: 2.5 seconds of damage reduction, ending in a 1-second fear on nearby enemies, and he can re-activate it early. A fear breaks a Chomp chain and walks Trundle off his own Frozen Domain — it is the single ability most likely to end a trade the page says Trundle wins. Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the target's maximum health and heals him for the damage dealt, which is why _missing-interactions.json raises resistances-invalidated here: stacking armour is the wrong answer, anti-heal is the right one.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl (15s): 2.5s damage reduction into a 1s fear. Jaws of the Beast: max-health damage that heals him.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0], wants.you[0], whys[0] and whys[3] all describe Chomp as an "AD steal" that rewards long fights, and spikes[1]/whys[4] describe Subjugate as stripping "half his resists".
audit.why: The AD sap is real, but the conclusion drawn from it is backwards while Jaws of the Beast is healing him for damage dealt off your maximum health — the longer the fight, the more he heals, until Grievous Wounds is on him. Subjugate takes 40%, not half, and the part that matters against a Heartsteel Warwick is the fifth of his maximum health it deals and heals.
audit.corrected: Short trades before anti-heal, long trades after. Subjugate: 40% of resists plus a fifth of max health.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gives Infinite Duress no figure and names nothing else; no cooldown number appears anywhere in the content layer.
audit.why: Infinite Duress 110/90/70s, Primal Howl 15/14/13/12/11s, Jaws of the Beast 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, Blood Hunt 80/70/60/50/40s, against Chomp's flat 3.5s. Two bites per Jaws is the trading rhythm, and Blood Hunt at 80 seconds at rank 1 is a cooldown he genuinely cannot re-use inside one laning trade.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], mid, late and two whys.

audit.why: wants.you[2] and report[8] both buy Executioner's Calling on the first back, which is exactly right for a kit with healing on the passive, the Q and the ultimate. The only fix needed was the ability name attached to it.
Both packet suspectNames are false positives: "Frozen Domain's" is a possessive and "Land Infinite Duress" is the correct name. The error in that line is the claim attached to it, not the spelling.

edits.before: Level 1 you are already the aggressor — Chomp on his first auto attempt steals a chunk of his AD and your King's Tribute heals you off every minion that dies nearby, so even losing a minion to him costs him more HP per trade than it costs you. Drop Frozen Domain at your feet the moment he steps up for a trade, not after: the movement speed and attack speed bonus hit immediately and you can chase down any retreat attempt. Pillar at level 3 is the real finisher — place it just behind him when he tries to disengage after a Chomp trade and he either eats one more full exchange or takes the knockup. He has no dash to clear terrain.
edits.after: Level 1 you are already the aggressor — Chomp on his first auto attempt saps a chunk of his AD and King's Tribute heals you off every minion that dies nearby, so even losing a minion to him costs him more health per trade than it costs you. Drop Frozen Domain at your feet the moment he steps up, not after: the movement and attack speed land immediately. Pillar at level 3 is the finisher — set it beside him as he disengages and he eats one more full exchange. Do not treat it as a cage, though: Jaws of the Beast is a dash, and Primal Howl fears you off him for a second every 15.

edits.before: Anti-heal is mandatory by your first back — Executioner's Calling at 800 gold cuts his Q and passive healing in half and turns every W-domain trade into a guaranteed HP lead for you. Trade strictly around his R cooldown: Infinite Duress is his only real kill threat, and it has a long cooldown at early ranks. When it is down, commit the full pattern: W down, Q-bite his AD, walk him down inside the zone. If he levels his W for the move speed, it does not matter inside Frozen Domain where you already out-speed and out-sustain him. Stay above 50% HP at all times — his passive heals him far harder when you are low, which is the only window a confident Warwick will dive.
edits.after: Anti-heal is mandatory by your first back — Executioner's Calling at 800 gold cuts Jaws of the Beast and Eternal Hunger and turns every domain trade into a guaranteed health lead. Trade around Infinite Duress: 110 seconds at rank 1, and his only real kill threat. Once it is spent, commit the full pattern — W down, Chomp his AD, walk him down inside the zone. Learn which half of his kit reads which health bar: Blood Hunt reads YOURS, switching on under 50% and tripling under 25%, while Eternal Hunger reads HIS, healing under 50% and tripling under 25%. Staying above half also denies his leap the bonus move speed it scales with.

edits.before: Subjugate is the matchup-closer: most Warwicks build into Heartsteel, Titanic, and some armor, meaning your R drains resists onto you and turns their own tanky itemization against them. In team fights, R their Warwick first before he R's your backline carry, then fight on your Frozen Domain while draining his resists — he becomes significantly less threatening the longer the fight goes. Two-item Warwick with Heartsteel stacks can start to outlast your Subjugate cooldown if you cannot maintain the domain fight, so end games before the 30-minute mark where his sustain scaling outpaces your stat-steal window.
edits.after: Subjugate is the matchup-closer: most Warwicks build Heartsteel, Titanic and some armour, so R takes 40% of those resists plus a fifth of his max health and heals you for the same amount. In team fights, Subjugate him before he leaps at your backline — Infinite Duress is 110s at rank 1 against your 120s, so he gets the first one — then fight on Frozen Domain while he wears the deficit. A two-item Warwick with Heartsteel stacks can outlast your R cooldown if you cannot hold the domain fight, so cash the lane lead into objectives before thirty minutes.

notes: The most useful thing on this page after the fix is the two-health-bars rule: Blood Hunt reads the enemy's health (on under 50%, tripled under 25%) and Eternal Hunger reads Warwick's own (heals under 50%, tripled under 25%). The page had merged them into one sentence pointing the wrong way, which produced the advice to fight a low-health Warwick. 'He has no dash to clear terrain' in `early` is flatly false — Jaws of the Beast is a dash and Infinite Duress is a leap — and it is the sort of claim that gets a player killed inside a pillar he thinks is a cage. Recurring across this slice: the phantom Pillar 'knockup' and 'strip half his resists' for a 40% steal.
